# Start Here: Step-by-Step Guide to Your Generated Files
### Build a RAG Agent in Copilot Studio | by Mayank Chugh

Follow the steps in order. Each step names the file, what to do, and when you are done.

## File map

| # | File | Role |
|---|------|------|
| 1 | `Copilot_RAG_Agent_YouTube_Episode_Plan.md` | What you teach: scope, timing, scenario |
| 2 | `Copilot_RAG_Agent_Source_Analysis.md` | Rights statement, conflicts, things to validate |
| 3 | `Copilot_RAG_Agent_Knowledge_Template.md` | Optional: add your real programme facts |
| 4 | `Copilot_RAG_Agent_Demo_Runbook.md` | What you execute: FAQ text, agent prompt, tests |
| 5 | `Copilot_RAG_Agent_Speaker_Script.md` | What you say |
| 6 | `Copilot_RAG_Agent_YouTube_Lecture.pptx` | What you show (8 slides with speaker notes) |
| 7 | `Copilot_RAG_Agent_Recording_Notes_and_Publishing_Pack.md` | Recording runbook, teaching notes, publishing pack, LinkedIn post |
| 8 | `Copilot_RAG_Agent_Improvements.docx` | Corrections, security, production readiness, learner misunderstandings |
| 9 | `mayank-youtube-content-SKILL-v5.md` | Your workflow for the next video |

All files for this episode are now created.

---

## Phase 1: Understand the episode (about 20 minutes)

### Step 1. Read the Episode Plan
- Check the title, audience, learning outcomes, scope and the 8-segment timing table.
- Note what is **not** included (topics and triggers, tools, publishing). That is Episode 2.
- **Done when:** you can state the episode goal in one sentence.

### Step 2. Read the Source Analysis
- Read the **Rights and originality** section first. It explains why nothing from the original course is reused.
- Read the **validation table**. It lists what to confirm on recording day: model names, licence needs, UI labels, and whether the Learn website source reaches Ready.
- **Done when:** you know which items you must check before you record.

### Step 3. Decide whether to use real facts (optional)
- Open the Knowledge Template.
- Either keep the sample FAQ in the Demo Runbook, or fill the template with your real programme answers.
- Leave fees, dates and prerequisites out if you want to demo the agent refusing.
- **Done when:** you have chosen sample or real content.

---

## Phase 2: Prepare the demo (about 60 to 90 minutes)

### Step 4. Work through the Demo Runbook
1. Copy the sample FAQ text into Word and save it as `AI_Pioneers_Demo_FAQ.docx`.
2. In Copilot Studio, create the agent with the name and description in section 1.
3. Paste the instructions from section 3.
4. Turn **open web search off**.
5. Upload the FAQ document, then add the Microsoft Learn website. Wait until both show **Ready**.
6. Run the four tests in section 4 and take a screenshot of each answer.
7. Complete the pre-recording validation in section 5.
- If an answer is off, adjust the instructions and re-test. Do not edit answers on camera.
- **Done when:** all four tests behave as expected and you have four rehearsal screenshots.

---

## Phase 3: Rehearse the delivery (about 45 minutes)

### Step 5. Read the Speaker Script aloud once
- Follow the timings and the **[SCREEN]** cues.
- Change any wording that doesn't sound like you.
- Keep the standard intro and outro.
- **Done when:** you can speak each segment without reading word for word.

### Step 6. Open the deck and check it, then skim the Improvements guide
- Read `Copilot_RAG_Agent_Improvements.docx` (3 pages): sections 1 and 10 matter most before recording.
- Open the PPTX in PowerPoint and look at all 8 slides, especially slide 5.
- Read the speaker notes. They point to the matching script segment.
- **Done when:** the slides match the script order and nothing is clipped.

---

## Phase 4: Record (about 60 to 90 minutes)

### Step 7. Prepare using the Recording Runbook
- Open `Copilot_RAG_Agent_Recording_Notes_and_Publishing_Pack.md` and read **Part A**.
- Set the screen to 1920x1080, silence notifications, and hide tenant and personal details.
- Open the script, instructions text and FAQ document on a second screen.

### Step 8. Record in this order
1. Demo segments first: build, knowledge, test.
2. Slide and talking segments: hook, problem, RAG, failure modes, takeaways.
3. Intro and outro last.
- If the website source is not Ready, say so, continue with the document, and show the rehearsal screenshot.
- **Done when:** you have clean takes of every segment.

---

## Phase 5: Publish and promote (about 45 minutes)

### Step 9. Use the Publishing Pack (Part C)
1. Pick a title, and set the thumbnail text.
2. Paste the description. Adjust the chapter timestamps to match your final edit.
3. Add **your own links** where the placeholder says so. Do not invent any.
4. Add the tags and the pinned comment.

### Step 10. Post on LinkedIn
- Use the LinkedIn post in Part C. Add your video link.

**Done when:** the video is published and the post is live.

---

## Phase 6: Next time

### Step 11. Reuse the workflow
- Give `mayank-youtube-content-SKILL-v5.md` to Claude with your next source folder.
- v5 adds the rights check, the demo-source rules, and the staged-delivery rule used in this project.
- Episode 2 idea: topics and triggers in Copilot Studio, built from your own scenario.

---

## Quick checklist before you hit record

- [ ] Both knowledge sources show Ready
- [ ] All four tests run and screenshots saved
- [ ] Web search is off
- [ ] UI labels match the script
- [ ] No model names or limits on slides
- [ ] Tenant and personal details hidden
- [ ] Sample FAQ will be labelled as sample on camera
